LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down again and sitting near its lowest point of the year, but nothing has changed about the business — it's the smallest of the big defense contractors and tends to trade at a discount, while military spending keeps rolling along steadily.

ASML.sentence: ASML has pulled back a fair bit from its high, which happens to this one from time to time — but they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, so the long-term story is intact.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet, which is exactly how this one works — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other gases under long contracts and nudge prices up a little each year, and investors have been leaning toward steady names like this lately.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm right now — its cloud business keeps renting out serious computing power for AI, and the next big update on how fast that's growing doesn't come until late January.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is sitting near its highs and having an uneventful week — they're the company that sells the equipment and supplies every lab needs, so they do steady business no matter which biotech wins.

CVX.sentence: Chevron dipped slightly, and the thing to remember is that its profits are puffed up right now by war-driven high oil prices rather than anything the company did, so it'll look cheaper than it really is until oil settles back toward normal.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen a long way from its peak even as big companies and government agencies keep signing multi-year deals for its workflow and AI-assistant tools — so the business is still growing fast while the stock has gotten noticeably cheaper.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore is holding up better than other mining names this week, which is exactly what you'd expect — besides digging up copper and nickel, they run the world's biggest commodity trading desk, which actually profits when prices get choppy.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is roughly flat; the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still creeping upward, which is the part that actually matters for this quarry business over time.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is flat, with the main headwind being a weakening Mexican peso, which shrinks the value of its Latin American sales when converted back to dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber ticked up and people keep booking more and more rides and food orders through the app; the one thing to keep watching is whether self-driving car companies choose to run on Uber's app or go it alone, which is a question about the future rather than a problem today.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk rose a bit and is trading below what its fleet of container ships would cost to replace — historically a sign the shipping cycle is near a low point, which for this global-trade bellwether tends to be a good entry level.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was essentially flat, and people keep tapping their cards more than ever — the gap between it and Visa has narrowed but there's no actual problem with the business.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company dipped slightly but is in its own usual buy range — hospitals keep performing more operations with its da Vinci machines, and every surgery means more single-use supplies sold.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell again as its biggest customers, Google's parent and Amazon, showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the difference — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but whether those customers can keep paying is the whole question.
